properties.title: Enhancing Personalized Bladder Cancer Treatment Through Reinforcement Learning: A Recurrent Patient State Transition Decision Support Framework

properties.name: Bladder1 Random-Forest transition simulator plus DQN policy
properties.membership: Core learned recurrent state-transition environment with simulation-trained controller; evidence reliability limited
properties.architecture: Two RF regressors update tumor size/count from current clinical state and onehot placebo/pyridoxine/thiotepa. MDP carries outputs across recurrent episodes;64/64dense DQN learns simulated return with replay and target network. Recurrent refers repeated state transitions, not recurrent-neural architecture.

properties.design: 118subject Bladder1 historical recurrent-event data; RF heldout metrics with insufficient split provenance; RL in learned simulated environment, no prospective treatment deployment.

assertions.rationale: Predicted tumor size/count become updated patient state used for subsequent episodes.
Current clinical state and recurrent episode enumeration condition transition.
Tumor size,count,recurrence and observation interval fields have explicit labels.
Three onehot treatment alternatives condition RF transition.
Treatment selection role separated from patient characteristics.
RF successor predictions advance recurrent treatment episodes.
Historical-data RF models approximate next size/count.
Two regressors emit interpretable successor tumor size/count.
Separate size/count prediction readouts used by reward.
MDP simulates successive actions and carries predicted state.
DQN learning samples transitions/rewards from learned simulation.
RF dynamics independent of DQN reward function, though printed rewarddefinitions conflict.
DQN is operational treatment-selection policy in simulated environment.
DQN selects actions autonomously in simulation, clinical final decisions explicitly reserved toclinician.
Treatment-conditioned predictions and simulated DQN treatment-return experiment reported.
RF regression errors for nexttumor size/count reported, but heldout protocol incompletely pinned.
DQN policy trained in learned environment and reported simulated reward.
Simulated actions alter patientstate supplied to nextDQN choice; no physical/clinical loop.

DQN simulatedreturn endpoint reported with uncertain reward/aggregation comparability. Evaluation is reported; this annotation does not establish a formal categorical acceptance outcome, so no pass/fail result is inferred.
Clinical featurevector and onehot treatment encoding formmodelinputs.
Train/test split described symbolically but patient boundaries and inputavailability unresolved.
criteria_missing: Reproducible fraction/seed, patient/time separation and future-feature exclusion

assertions.rationale: Named treatment categories/start-stop times exist, but dose/route and executable administration regimen absent.
Multiagentarchitecture discussed onlyas futureextension; no distinct co-ordinating agents implemented.
Real-timeclinical inputs and onlinelearning are explicitly future research.
Patient-specific onlineweightadaptation not implemented; RL training isoffline simulation, not newpatientmeasurement adaptation.

assertions.applicability_reason: No prospective care/workflow evaluation; alltreatmentreturns arelearned-environment simulation.

evidence_fragments.content:
To emulate patient -specific disease progression within this 
sequential environment, a predictive state -transition module 
is learned from historical clinical observations. In the current 
implementation, Random Forest regressors are employed to 
estimate changes in tumor size and tumor count, allowing the 
framework to approximate subsequent patient states 
following each treatment decision. Rather than serving as the 
primary contribution, these predictive models function as 
transition approximators within the simulation environment, 
enabling repeated evaluation of treatment trajectories under 
different clinical scenarios. The simulated patient trajectories 
provide the reinforcement learning agent with an interactive 
environment in which treatment strategies can be iteratively 
evaluated and refined to optimize sequential decision -
making. Cumulative changes in tumor size and tumor count 
serve as performance indicators, guiding the agent toward 
treatment policies that minimize long -term tumor 
progression. Figure 1 p resents an overview of the proposed 
decision-support framework and the overall study workflow.

throughout the simulation process.

The Q-Network was trained for 100 episodes, as this duration 
was sufficient for learning, as evidenced by the results and 
analysis section. A batch size of 32 was used to sample mini-
batches from the replay buffer, helping stabilize training by 
reducing va riance and improving convergence. The 
optimizer employed a learning rate of α=0.001, controlling 
the step size for gradient updates. The replay buffer, with a 
capacity of 10,000, stored past experiences (s, a, r, s'), 
allowing each training step to sample a batch of experiences 
to minimize correlations between consecutive samples and 
enhance learning stability. To further stabilize training, the 
target network was updated every 10 episodes, 
synchronizing its weights with the Q -network. This Q -
Network and DQ N framework enable sequential decision -
making in bladder cancer treatment by selecting actions 
(treatment choices) that maximize cumulative future 
rewards, supporting an effective and data -driven treatment 
strategy.

Algorithm 3: Experience Replay Sampling 
Objective: 
Enhance model stability and improve learning by 
uniformly sampling past experiences for model training, 
reducing the risk of overfitting to recent events. 
Inputs: 
• A replay buffer containing past experiences in 
the format of states, actions, rewards, next states, 
and completion flags. 
• Batch size, which specifies the number of 
experiences to sample at each step. 
Outputs: 
• A structured batch of sampled experiences ready 
for model training. 
Procedure: 
1. Sample Experiences from Buffer: Select a set 
number of past experiences from the replay 
buffer, ensuring each experience is unique and 
represents diverse scenarios. 
2. Organize Batch Components: Extract each 
experience component separately (states, 
actions, rewards, next states, and done flags) and 
organize them into structured arrays, which helps 
maintain consistency in model input and output. 
3. Convert Arrays to PyTorch Tensors: Prepare 
each array for model training by converting them 
into tensors. Continuous variables (states, next 
states, rewards) are converted to float tensors, 
while discrete variables (actions, done flags) use 
integer or binary representations. 
4. Return Tensors: The organized tensors are now 
ready for use in model training, providing a 
balanced representation of past experiences to 
refine the model’s predictive accuracy. 
 
End Algorithm 
 
D. DQN Training Loop 
The training loop of the Deep Q -Network (DQN) model is 
designed to iteratively adjust the neural network parameters, 
optimizing treatment actions for patients to maximize the 
reduction in tumor size and count. Each episode simulates a 
complete cycle of pat ient interactions, where the model 
learns to predict outcomes of selected treatments and refines 
itself based on the cumulative rewards obtained.  For each 
patient, an initial state S includes features such as tumor 
count number, tumor size size, recurrence recur, start time 
start, and stop time stop. These features are encoded into a 
vector for the neural network. Action selection follows an 
epsilon ϵ-greedy policy, balancing exploration and 
exploitation. An action A (treatment selection) is chosen 
with probability epsilon ϵ for a random action or 1−ϵ for the 
action maximizing the predicted reward. The selected 
treatment action is applied, resulting in updated tumor size 
and count values. After applying a treatment, the reward R is 
computed based on the reduction in tumor size and count, 
𝑅 = (𝑡𝑢𝑚𝑜𝑟 𝑠𝑖𝑧𝑒 𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑔𝑒) + (𝑡𝑢𝑚𝑜𝑟 𝑐𝑜𝑢𝑛𝑡 𝑐ℎ𝑎𝑛𝑔𝑒) (17) 
A new state S′ is created based on the updated patient 
characteristics post -treatment. The experience tuple 
(S,A,R,S′,done) is stored in the replay buffer, where "done" 
indicates whether this is the last treatment in the sequence.
